This is a re-submission. All the [updated] info is in this Google Doc:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1X0ESIB854-dv1m-whpJyt9KIeas-24qhT7M9GYwMjTM/

Missing criteria pointed out by the reviewers have been addressed, namely:
1) The scientific blogs: we now have 3 of them published post Fund9 acceptance.
2) A section about technologies used and the reasoning was extended in the Google Doc.
3) The register page is now fully functional on PubWeave.

The only part that has not been addressed is the monthly technical blogs. We felt comfortable postponing these for a few reasons:
- We wished to focus on the development on the blog section of PubWeave.
- We wanted to use PubWeave to publish our technical blogs for marketing purposes.
- Writing the blogs is a tiny fraction of the resources used for building the website (1-2% of the funds were going to go to writing the blogs), so we assumed it was fair to ask the community to let us postpone them until after PubWeave is ready, which is very soon! (You can go see for yourselves: https://pubweave.intellart.ca).

To make up for the 3 blogs that were missed during that period, we are going to be writing them bi-weekly for the next 3 months, so that the total amount of blog articles is unchanged. And they will be published on PubWeave! We thank the reviewers in advance for their consideration.

ms.promise:
Everything up to this point has been built and connected together, time to work out the kinks, test smart-contract functionalities and deploy on testnet.
Our experience with our current ongoing project (Veritheum, as of October 2022) has indicated that this step of the process (testing and setting up) needs a significant chunk of project development time and funds. This is when surprises happen and where planning is as simple as deciding to keep funds on the side to be able to get to the finish line.
As such, it is hard to predict at this time what the details of the outputs will look like. Globally, we should get a functioning dApp on testnet.
Additionally, a big chunk of funds will be allocated to social media growth and outreach. Outputs include public events attended, potential on-boarded users and social media traction.

ms.report:
New content: Following the reviewer's comments regarding the tokenomics model, we have added a blog article that serves as a sequel to the previous article and contains a detailed description of its different components: https://www.pubweave.com/blog/revenue_sharing_model_publishing.
Update: This resubmission simply adds a comment to today's reviewer's decision. First of all, we thank you for your comments and due diligence on the matter. Second, we would like to state that we have absolutely no problem submitting a change request, as we have done so in the past. However, we do not see how a change request is applicable -- here's why: The deliverable clearly stated that a research-based tokenomics model would be submitted, with NO mention of a token launch. We never promised to launch a token, but only to formalize a tokenomics model and how it would fit with the rest of the industry, because we were never sure if this was a road we want to go down. Our first PoA submission for this milestone stated that we finally decided not to launch a token in the foreseeable future, and that prompted us to skip the tokenomics design. As requested by the reviewer, and we agreed, the tokenomics model was part of the milestone, which is why it ended up being part of our last submission a few days ago (A theoretical tokenomics model for Open Science). Now that we have completed it, we do not see any variation from the deliverables list. As mentioned, it is not clear to us what a change request would entail, but if the reviewer still judges that it needs to be submitted, we will of course do so. However, we would greatly appreciate a prompt reply and acceptance of this PoA to be able to move on and wrap up this project as soon as possible. Thank you for your cooperation.
